data.text:

WHAT IS THIS TOOTHPASTE LIKE?
This toothpaste is not a white paste more of a paste gel. It has a really nice mojito flavor that is not sweet but still tastes good at the same time. There is a flip top on it and the tube is plastic.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
I have used it for half the tube now and it seems to help with sensitive teeth. I also feel that it cleans the teeth well too.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I like this toothpaste/gel. It tastes good, is unusual, but seems to work well for my sensitive teeth.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS so far. This is a nice product. I would probably buy again if it continues to perform well over time. I have two more tubes to go through. I will update if anything changes.

data.title: No Floride, Good for Whitening Your Teeth
data.text:
This is an interesting product - the instructions make it seem complicated because you're supposed to rinse your mouth out with the toothpaste foam first, before adding it to a toothbrush and then brushing. I'm not sure why you need to put it in your mouth twice - there is no explanation for this other than it helps use up the foam faster, which means you'll have to buy a new one before long.

I just ignore this step and spray the foam directly onto the brush and then brush. It has a pleasant taste. It did whiten my tea-stained teeth a little.

Now, there is no fluoride in this toothpaste, so it doesn't take care of gingivitis or plaque. All it has is baking soda. As a result, I will use this as a supplement to my usual Colgate Total. Overall it's a good product but I can't use it by itself because of the lack of fluoride, which prevents cavities.

data.title: Too Gentle and Mild
data.text: This Spotlight toothpaste says it's vegan and claims to rebuild enamel but I showed this to my dentist and she was skeptical. She recommends Sensodyne which has much stronger ingredients to fight tooth decay and eroding enamel. I suspected as much - I didn't like the texture of this toothpaste and though it does have fluoride (thank goodness), I don't feel the same sensation of cleanliness I get with Colgate Total or Sensodyne. It feels very mild and there is no foaming action. There are many obscure toothpastes like these on the market that claim to be "healthier" but I have yet to find any equivalent to what's already working for me. Oh well.

data.title: Non-Fluoride Toothpaste with Ginger Root Extract and Aloe Vera
data.text:
According to the manufacturer, "Fresh Aid Toothpaste is packed with quality ingredients that target gum diseases like gingivitis and plaque. It prevents tooth decay and gum and tooth pain. It's also the best toothpaste for those with sensitive teeth and gums."

This toothpaste has ginger root extract, which I can taste and may partially account for the tingling sensation that stays on after you rinse your mouth out. The toothpaste has a yellowish color and kind of reminds me of lemon filling. It leaves your mouth feeling fairly clean but there is a lightness to this toothpaste that other white and chalky toothpastes (like Crest) don't have.

I question whether the lack of fluoride will be effective in the long-term at protecting my recessed gums and preventing plaque from taking hold. I usually use Colgate Total, so only time will tell if this toothpaste will be as effective. I have been brushing it now for only a week, so I will update this review if anything changes. For now, it's an OK toothpaste for those who are concerned with the amount of chemicals in their toothpaste. Because of my gum issues, effectiveness is more of a priority for me, so if you have overall healthy teeth and gums, you may love it.

data.title: Good But Black Colored Toothpaste Takes Getting Used To
data.text:
I liked the minty taste of this toothpaste (despite the name, it doesn't taste like charcoal at all) but the black color takes a bit of getting used to.

When you spit out the toothpaste, it looks as if you're spitting out mud and if you're wearing something light colored it will stain. The second thing is that the packaging is deceptively larger than the actual product - once I opened the box, I was disappointed to find that each tube is small - no bigger than the size of a "deluxe" sample or travel-sized toothpaste. Good for TSA regulations but stingy if you're wanting to use it at home. So, while it leaves my breath smelling fresh, I'm not sure I'd buy it again, for aesthetic as well as quantity reasons.

data.title: Works as well as other sensitive toothpastes, but not thrilled with the taste or consistency
data.text:
This has a 5% concentration of potassium nitrate, which is the ingredient used in all sensitive toothpastes to cut down (or, in my case, eliminate) sensitive teeth issues. As such, it works the same as other sensitive toothpastes.

It does differ from others with regard to taste and consistency. It has a mild minty taste that, while acceptable, is not all that fresh tasting. The consistency is a bit softer than other toothpastes and it doesn't foam up as much. While that's usually a plus, good foaming action is a benefit when it comes to sensitive toothpastes since it helps the potassium nitrate get into all the nooks and crannies. My favorite sensitive toothpaste is the Colgate foaming action one. It has the same 5% potassium nitrate as this, but the foaming action does make a difference.

While the tube looks big, there's not a lot of product. It's only filled about 1/2 of the way and, while it looks like a standard size tube, it only provides 3.5 oz of toothpaste. It's also hard to get all of it out of the tube since the tube is plastic and does not roll up. It dispenses fine when mostly full, but is not great at dispensing when the level gets low.

While this does work, the negatives put my score at 3 stars (average). Not a compelling purchase compared with other options.

data.title: Mildly minty flavor, minimal whitening.
data.text:
This is a "vegan friendly" toothpaste with a mildly minty flavor that is reminiscent of peppermint. The mildness means it doesn't have the sting that some other brands have. This MAY also help prevent sensitivity issues that occur with other whitening toothpastes.

As for the actual whitening qualities, after using it for a week (2x daily) I've noticed SLIGHT whitening effects, but nothing dramatic.

It DOES leave your mouth feeling fresh after brushing however, and my teeth feel "smooth" after brushing.

The active ingredient is sodium fluoride at 0.24%, which is exactly the amount in other toothpastes I compared it to.

On another note, there is a considerable amount of air in the tube (so it takes a little pressure to release that first squirt).

Overall, I'd say this is a decent toothpaste that is mild, and whitens slightly, but it's also pricey, and not much different than any drugstore brand of whitening toothpaste.

data.title: I Like This Toothpaste BUT It Doesn't Treat Sensitivity As Advertised
data.text:
I ordered this because I'm currently using this brands whitening system & wanted a toothpaste that would help with sensitivity as well as remineralization. The thing is, it says nothing about desensitizing or hypersensitivity. I took off a star for that.

The title at the time of ordering & of my review:
"Spotlight Oral Care Toothpaste for Total Care | Prevents Cavities & Desensitizes Hypersensitivity | Vegan & Gluten-Free | Active Ingredients of Fluoride & Pentasodium Triphosphate"

I'm middle aged & have need to strengthen my enamel. I normally use Sensodyne for enamel repair. I like this toothpaste better than Sensodyne. I also use the generic "Act" remineralizing mouthwash at least twice a day. So far, I can't really say if any of it is actually helping.

Anyway, this toothpaste has a nice clean minty taste that isn't too strong & it doesn't have that crazy rabid dog foam. The price right now is about double what it was when I first looked at it. I'm not sure what the deal is there. I'd suggest keeping an eyeball on it & nab it when the price is a bit more realistic as it's not worth paying $10 for a 3.5oz tube of toothpaste.

data.title: Natural Lemon Toothpaste =D
data.text:
I really like this toothpaste. I've tried a heck of a lot of various natural toothpastes over the past 2 decades & thankfully have liked a heck of a lot of them. I decided to try this brands "The Freshest Mouth" Mild Spearmint & this Mojito "Healthy Teeth & Gum Care" toothpaste. Out of the two, I like this toothpaste much more. Don't get me wrong, I like the spearmint well enough, I just like this better.

Like many natural toothpastes, this doesn't have a ridiculous amount of foam. It doesn't feel abrasive at all. It also doesn't irritate the flesh inside of my mouth. I love the light lemony flavor as well.

If you like a strong flavored toothpaste you probably wont be happy with this. There are other natural brands that have a lot more essential oils. If you are looking for something mild, you are going to love this brand.

data.title: Maybe not for crowns?
data.text:
Nice to try, won't buy this brand again, but would be interested in trying another.

In the morning I feel a little build up behind the back of my bottom teeth (where my tongue touches) and on the cheek side of my molars (which are porcelain crowns). I've been wondering if perhaps when I finish brushing I should mix the used paste with hot water then gargle with it to better reach all areas of my mouth? Maybe that would help with the bacteria growth from my tongue? Maybe I'll try an organic mouthwash and see if that helps.

The taste is gross, but after several days I don't notice it anymore.
Also, spitting out the brownish residue was a touch off putting at first because I couldn't tell if my gums were bleeding or not.

I have noticed that my gums aren't as sensitive as usual, don't bleed as much when I floss, and seem less cold sensitive.
My teeth don't seem any whiter, but they are shiny after brushing (as expected).
I have noticed that my mouth isn't sore from brushing anymore, and I don't find skin strings in my mouth in the morning.

Buuuuut, I'm not so sure this toothpaste works for crowns. I notice my real teeth feel very clean (and stay clean) but my crowns always feel dirty on the chewing surfaces. Perhaps the porcelain has been scratched from the normal toothpaste and that's that I'm feeling?

I also don't like how the coconut oil coats my toothbrush and bristles and makes it harder to clean and sterilize.

EDITED: I forgot to mention two things:

First, I'm not sure how, or if, this has helped to freshen my breath, but I haven't noticed a bad breath or a fresh breath smell either.

Second, because of the coconut oil the container leaves a ring on my counter and drips oil down the sides. .

It's now been two weeks since I quit using it and the sides of my tongue are still raw and swollen, my gums (especially around the edges of my teeth) still burn, throb, and ache constantly, my teeth have become very sensitive, and there's a bloody, metallic taste in my mouth all the time.  I'm afraid this toothpaste from hell has caused permanent damage.  If anyone knows how to reverse the effects or how long it takes to heal after using this stuff, please let me know, because it's really beginning to scare me.

data.text: During Covid concerns I certainly did not want to go to the dentist and have people right in my face so I had a serious issue when a dental problem arose.  It felt like my four bottom front teeth were going to fall out. They hurt a lot and I could not figure out why.  No cavities there of course and no receding gums.  They just plain hurt - especially when I brushed them.  A friend suggested I try a toothpaste for sensitive teeth.  And so I tried this.  Within three days the pain had diminished and within three weeks it was gone.  I was amazed. This product saved my teeth and me a lot of money for a dental appointment. data.title: Blech!
data.text: I've used toothpaste with activated charcoal.  I know what clove tastes like and have even used pure clove oil to help with a toothache, so the taste isn't unfamiliar to me.  But for whatever reason, the combination of the two in this toothpaste was the most awful thing I've ever tasted!  The only reason I can give it two stars rather than one is because the charcoal did what it was supposed to and scrubbed up my teeth.  Even if the foam did look like I'd been bobbing for apples in the local sewage treatment plant.  However, I can get the same kind of tooth cleaning from charcoal toothpastes which taste much, MUCH better. (Actually, I'll get a better tooth and mouth cleaning with a toothpaste I want to use for more than five seconds, especially when I don't want to gag when I brush my tongue.)  I'll donate the other two tubes I've got - maybe somebody else will enjoy them - but the rest of the first tube will be going in the trash, as much as it pains me to waste stuff.  Because thanks, but no thanks - yuck!

Also, they are bulky. For example, I wanted to use the small one on a tube of eyelid primer but the tube squeezer was so much bigger than the primer tube that I couldn't get it in my makeup drawer.

data.title: A good toothpaste
data.text: I received a free full size sample of this product to review. The opinions expressed in this review are 100% my own. After using Crest-Pro health toothpaste for two weeks, my teeth definitely feel much cleaner and more polished. It leaves my breath fresh and clean feeling for hours after using it. However, I don't prefer the taste over other brands. The taste is somewhat strong and a bit too minty for me (even if not a lot of tooth paste is used). I prefer a spearmint type taste over the taste of this toothpaste. My fiancé is also using the toothpaste and he has commented that his teeth also feel more polished after using it. He prefers the taste of this toothpaste over other brands. So as for taste, it's all a matter of preference. As for sensitivity protection, I don't notice much of a difference between this and Sensodyne, so I suppose it's pretty good. I also use Crest Classic Whitestrips, so my teeth are already very white. The toothpaste seems to maintain the whiteness of my teeth really well. I have a dentist appointment in less than a week for a 6 month cleaning...we'll see what the dental hygienist has to say about my teeth then!

data.title: an average, middle-of-the-road toothpaste when compared to name-brand sensitive toothpastes
data.text:
Review of: Spotlight Oral Care Toothpaste for Sensitive Teeth

I’ve been using the Spotlight Oral Care Toothpaste for the last week or so and, so far at least, I’ve been pleased with the product.

I found that the taste of the toothpaste is actually pretty good, especially in comparison to other ‘fresh mint’ flavored toothpastes I’ve tried before that seem to have an off-taste or bitter after-taste them. The mint taste of the Spotlight is present but not overwhelming; which I like.

The foaming action of the toothpaste I consider to be about average; certainly, enough in my estimation to feel as if the toothpaste was getting to every corner of my mouth but not so much as to be annoying.

The active ingredients I also consider to be about average for a decent quality ‘sensitive’ toothpaste; Potassium Nitrate and Sodium Fluoride. And, after using the product a few times now, I consider the effectiveness (based on the potassium nitrate level of 5.0%) to be about the same as many other ‘sensitive’ toothpastes I’ve tried in the past.

After brushing, the Spotlight toothpaste does leave my teeth feeling clean and does leave my mouth with a nice, somewhat minty taste.

For me, while this toothpaste is noticeably better than some bargain-basement type sensitive toothpastes, it is roughly equal to many quality, name-brand or store-brand toothpastes.

The cost, however, for this 3.5 ounce tube of sensitive toothpaste is a concern for me as I consider it to be on the higher side; especially for what I rate as an average, middle-of-the-road toothpaste.

data.title: Plastic tensioner tabs broke off right away.  But worked anyway.
data.text:
Got a package with three of these toothpaste tube squeezers.
It was easy to insert the bottom of the tube into the twist key and then push that into the base. My tube was pretty full, so I only got a partial wrap, but it seemed to be working good.
The base can be used to sit the tube upright on the counter and that worked.

Two days later I was able to get another half twist out of the key. Then one of the plastic tabs on bottom of unit broke. Then I just thought I would try to twist it just a bit and the other tab broke off.
In case it was just one defective unit I tried another one and it broke also. If they are breaking off with only one wrap of tube, there is no way this can work for even half a tube.

I then just tried pushing on the tension tabs with my finger to see how much flex they had. The answer is almost none. There is no way these tabs will not break off.

However, I kept using this and to my surprise it worked anyway. I didn't think the wrapped tube would fit in the space, but it did. So I am adding a picture with tube wrapped up and almost empty. So I bumped this up from 1 to 3 stars. With all the tensioner taps all breaking off, I don't think I should rate it any higher.

It makes it convenient to use when premixed and keeps me in the creative flow. The tubes are small so make sure when pouring your mix into them tou leave enough room to crimp and seal the bottom. The tubes themselves are a tad flimsy, meaning the aluminum is thin and easy to puncture. Many of the tubes arrived slightly wrinkled making the over look, once complete, unpolished, which as a professional artist and workshop facilitator isn't desireable. For these reasond, and the fact that there was a few days of delay in shipping, even though I purchased them as a 2-day shipping period via a prime member, is the reason I felt three stars was fair. What I liked about this product was that I didn't have to buy a case and it does allow me to premix paint, also making it easier for me to prepare for my workshops in advance. I do think I'll try a few more brands before purchasing again to learn if there are long tubes with thicker aluminum out there. All and all these do serve a purpose.

data.title: Try it!
data.text: This is the first time that I have used a toothpaste that comes out of its container in the form of foam.  In my mind it provides almost like a combination of toothpaste and mouthwash sort of feeling in my mouth.  I really like it, plus it has a pleasant spearmint taste to it, very refreshing.  It is designed to repair gums, remove stains, and prevent tooth decay.  If it can do all that, I will be very pleased indeed.  In the meantime I am enjoying the novelty, at least for me, of this product which fills my mouth with a healthful dose of foam,  containing ingredients that are known to be good for dental health:  Glycerol, Citrus Junos Extract, Xylitol, Baking Soda, and Essence of Mint. There is nothing artificial among the ingredients, as far as I can tell.  The product is also a good way to keep my breath smelling fresh.  I suggest shaking the bottle gently before each use, and storing it in a cool, dry place, away from direct sunlight.  I look forward to using this teeth-whitening foam, made in Ireland,  in the days ahead.  It's a fun experience to use it.  Do check with your dentist first if you like.

data.text: I purchased it for what it can do, NOT for any fancy flavor.  It’s almost tasteless so if you’re looking for something to taste sweet or fruity in order to use it, don’t buy this!  It’s a nice change.  And it cleans WELL!  This was a good purchase.  Just know that the key to getting it onto your brush with minimal waste is lightly wet your toothbrush, hold it over the opened jar, then sprinkle the fine powder onto it.  As you brush and have to spit, remember that it contains charcoal so when start rinsing your mouth in the sink, there will be some temporary staining of the charcoal.  However, it removes really easy.  Just run the water over those areas and it’s gone!  This is a joy to use because so little of it goes a long way.  The amount in that scooper that comes with it is all you need.  A level amount, not a heaping mound of it.

data.title: Smooths, whitens, reduces gum inflammation! Almost no taste.
data.text:
I've never used this as I was always hesitant about how it would taste. It has almost no taste (a little chalky) & the way I use it, it doesn't get on my tongue much.

I rub it on with a finger, in a polishing motion, over all the surfaces of my teeth I can get to for just about 20 seconds. Then, I use my Water Pik to get it out of all the nooks & crannies. If you miss even a little, your teeth will look like the Wicked Witch's!

Instantly, after just one use, my teeth felt smoother & cleaner than even after using my electric toothbrush & Water Pik. I still use my toothbrush for my gums & to use my fluoride toothpaste.

Every few hours, I rub it into my teeth. I don't add water. My saliva is enough as you want it to be a thick paste. Now, after only a week, my teeth are looking brighter & whiter. My dentist noticed before I told him about it. He was very positive about the use of charcoal powder.

An added awesome bonus: When I've had an irritation of the gums, I've rubbed it in, let it sit for about a minute, then washed it out. It has reduced & even eliminated the inflammation & pain!

data.title: Thick Consistency, Not Much Lather
data.text:
Spotlight Oral Care Toothpaste for Total Care is packaged and priced like a higher end toothpaste, so I thought I would give it a try. Maybe I’m just used to toothpastes like Colgate, but this toothpaste has a strangeness factor to it that I haven’t adjusted to yet. I don’t hate it, but I don’t love it either.

The first thing I noticed is that it is thicker than any toothpaste I’ve ever used. I have to work at it to get just a little out of the tube onto my toothbrush. The consistency is somewhere between toothpaste and caulking. The second thing I noticed is that it doesn’t suds or lather much at all. I’ve never experienced that before. I wondered how well it could be cleaning without hardly any sudsing. If you are a messy brusher, this might be a plus. The third thing is the flavor. When they say mint flavor, they mean mint. I get the mint tingle through my whole mouth and lips. I’m talking about the Blistex tingle, not a mild tingle. It’s a bit too much for my tastes.

All that said, when I do finish with my rather unique brushing experience, my teeth do feel very clean, more so than with my regular toothpaste. The clean feeling also lasts longer. I do think this toothpaste is overpriced for one that doesn’t contain whiteners. It’s ingredients are aimed at cavity prevention and plaque buildup, which are basic toothpaste functions. While it seems to work at cleaning my teeth, I don’t think I would get this again.

data.title: Information on the mouth film from Crest
data.text:
It took me a really long time to determine that this toothpaste is what causes the mouth slime/scum/film in my mouth. But, I didn't want to just speculate. So, I located some information on Crest's own website:

"Q: Since using Pro-Health toothpaste, I've noticed a "shedding" of the lining of my mouth. It is like a layer peels off each time I use it. My mouth feels cleaner than ever, but I'm not sure if this is normal."

"A: The shedding that you have noticed in your mouth is not unsafe and is a result of the natural process to remove dead cells from the skin surfaces in your mouth. The cleaning action of both Crest Pro-Health Toothpaste and Crest Pro-Health Rinse can accelerate this process and often results in the skin coming off in sheets, making the removal of dead skin cells more noticeable."

[...]

I've been using Crest for the majority of my life and have had almost zero cavities. So, I'll continue buying Crest, but I will NOT be buying 'Pro Health' any longer.

data.title: Taste is good, works well
data.text:
I haven't used a lot of non fluoride toothpastes but I've been wanting to switch and this brand seemed good because I am a fan of Tea Tree oil. The paste is translucent, almost clear and has a fresh minty taste to it. Abrasive particles are used to clean deposits off teeth and gums and it works well with my Sonicare brush.

The tube is a bit smaller than other brands I've used but you only need a small amount as it's very strong. I overwhelmed myself the first time I used it and was sneezing for a few minutes from one of the ingredients. I reduced the amount of paste I used and that didn't happen again so I have no side effects to report when used properly. Good product, and a nice alternative to fluoride toothpastes.

data.title: Mild flavors, but not for my toddler
data.text: Every parent knows that brushing a toddler's teeth is a battle. We have 5 different toothbrushes, and this is our 3rd toothpaste in hopes of finding a miraculous flavor that will make my toddler put up less of a fight. We've been using Orajel toddler toothpaste for some time, but we were thinking the gel consistency was uncomfortable for our child, so we decided to give this foam version a try. Well...he doesn't necessarily hate it, but as soon as he sees the foam dispensing, I think he associates it with bath foam, and he constantly tries to touch it, which makes it difficult to use. When we actually get it in his mouth, he seems to hate the texture. I don't think it's necessarily the flavor or the taste, because I tried it, and it's so mild that I don't think it would bother him. Then again, he's a 16-month old still navigating communicating his feelings. We put it on hold for now, but we may reintroduce it to him again in a few months.

data.title: Sickeningly sweet and ineffective
data.text:
As an adult who cannot stomach the strong taste of adult toothpaste, others often tease me for my tendency to use children's toothpaste. While I love some of the toothpastes I have tried, this is not one of them.

Like many children's gel toothpastes, this does not foam very well. Unlike many, it's taste it not overpowering, probably because the taste is gone a few seconds after you start brushing - like cheap bubblegum. And like cheap bubblegum, you'll continue to taste the disgusting flavour until you're done brushing (or chewing) and even afterward as it will stick in your mouth.

Overall, this doesn't leave your mouth and teeth feeling very refreshed or cleansed and doesn't do much for your breath either. There are better toothpaste products on the market for children (and adults).

data.title: Mouth Slime Galore!!!
data.text: I gave this toothpaste two stars only because it does clean your mouth, but also creates mouth slime galore! I had been using the toothpaste for about two months. About a month ago, I noticed I started getting this slimy substance inside my mouth. It would occur all day long, and I could gather/pull out huge gobs of slime!!! It was embarrassing. The inside of my mouth never hurt. No sores of any kind, just alot of white slime. One day my fiance noticed some on the outside corner of my mouth that had somehow escaped from the inside! That's when I realized I needed to research the cause. I was worried it might be thrush or something serious, but didn't think so because I didn't have any pain or sores. I'm not on any medication, so I knew it couldn't be the result of a side effect. Searching the internet I found lots of people with the same condition, and we all had something in common. We used Crest Pro Health toothpaste!!! Interestingly enough, my fiance uses it also and has never had a problem with it. But I'm going to stop using it immediately, and see what happens. I have to assume this is the cause since it only started after I changed from my old toothpaste (Aquafresh) to Crest Pro Health.

data.title: GREAT for people with sensitive teeth.
data.text:
I received a free sample of Crest Pro-Health Whitening Toothpaste for the purpose of my review. Opinions are 100% my own. I have extremely sensitive teeth that causes me to experience severe sensitivity pain to cold air or cold liquid. This is not from cavities. I have been examined by a dentist. Normally, if I have not used my prescription toothpaste and use non-prescription toothpaste, the sensitivity pain comes back with a vengeance within three days. I mean the kind of pain that brings you to your knees.

After using Crest Pro-Health gel toothpaste for five days, I have not experienced any sensitivity pain whatsoever. Plus, the taste is a refreshing cool mint. It is nice and foamy which I like. My teeth are clean after brushing. I don't see any whitening effects at this time, but it has only been five days.

I primarily like this product for controlling my sensitive teeth. The mint taste, foam and whitening (I guess if used long enough) are added bonuses. I give it four stars because I don't see any whitening effects at this time.

Cons: My one gripe with this toothpaste is the whitening. Everyone wants white teeth and this product claims to give them to you. I just don’t find this to be the case and I’ve used it for almost two years. I sub in a whitening mouthwash when I feel I need it to compensate for the lack of whitening the toothpaste does but I do wish I didn’t have to.

Overall I will keep using this but I’m always looking out for a better whitening option!

data.title: Checks all the boxes for me!
data.text: I was happy to find a sensitive toothpaste that was made in the USA of natural ingredients and actually works! I have been using it for a week now and so far I m happy! It has helped with my sensitive tooth pain and makes my whole mouth feel clean! This toothpaste has a natural mint flavor that I dig, it leaves my mouth smelling and tasting clean without a sour aftertaste like I get from Stannous Fluoride does. Typically you will find either Potassium Nitrate or Stannous Fluoride as the active ingredient in sensitive toothpastes. Whenever I use toothpaste with Stannous Fluoride, my mouth is left with a sour after taste that makes me feel like my breath is bad even after a through brushing. Not the case with this Spotlight Oral Care Toothpaste, it has Potassium Nitrate and Sodium Fluoride instead. It works to calm tooth pain and still leaves my mouth fresh! As is the case with most natural style toothpastes, this one does not create huge amounts of lather, but it still does a good job of cleaning. it gets the job done without any unnecessary additives. Plus it is made in the USA and comes in a recyclable tube which I appreciate! All in all, I am happy and I would purchase this again for my sensitive teeth!

data.title: Kills gums
data.text:
I started using my husband's toothpaste (the product listed on this page) when my Sensodyne Repair and Protect ran out. It seemed okay at first, so I didn't bother replacing my Sensodyne. What a mistake.

As mentioned, this toothpaste was fine for a week or two. Suddenly I developed a sore area on the small web of skin/muscle that connects the bottom lip area to the bottom gum. Despite using Orajel, it continued getting worse and is now a nice white dot of pain. Brushing my teeth with this Crest toothpaste was like applying acid to this area and it made me procrastinate about brushing my teeth altogether.

I only really connected the sore with the toothpaste today when I decided to get some more of my regular Sensodyne, and man was it a difference. I was able to brush the sore softly without it stinging too much. It already feels a lot better than it has done these past few days.

I didn't really experience the "slime" I have seen mentioned a lot here, but that's possibly because I use mouthwash right after brushing.

Either way, would not recommend this to anyone who values their gums.

data.title: Actually Works.
data.text: So I bought this Fine Powdered Charcoal because I have been seeing all the posts across social media about how charcoal can whiten your teeth, and Wow, it really does. I have noticed a big big difference in how white my teeth have become and this product is food grade. To be honest, this stuff is really messy. So the instructions say to wet the toothbrush and dip it into the powdered charcoal and brush your teeth. I tried this first and I did notice a slight difference in coloring. My biggest problem was the texture. I did not like having that powder in my mouth. It was so dry that it wasn't comfortable. So I decided to experiment with the charcoal and toothpaste. It is so much better. What I did was I took a tube of brand name  toothpaste which I had bought from Dollar Tree and combine that with a few tablespoons of charcoal. I tried to blend it as best I could and added a splash of mouthwash to smooth the texture. It turned out wonderful. I had my best friend try my experiment and I had him try the powder. We both agree that the experiment is more successful because it is the closest thing to actually brushing your teeth normally. it is still kinda messy so I would recommend to brush using the charcoal while in the shower. I typically use the charcoal first and then I go back over it with a regular toothpaste. Because the charcoal doesn't freshen your breath. Even my experiment doesn't freshen breath. The purpose of my experiment was to make the charcoal easier to brush with. Next topic is a charcoal face mask. This application of charcoal was kinda a bust because I don't think it worked. To make the mask, mix 2 teaspoons of charcoal with pure water /rose water/aloe gel to make a paste. Apply to face and let dry. Gently wash off. It had two optional ingredients which were coconut oil and honey. I tried it with just water and it didn't seems to do much. Worse of all, I couldn't get all of it off. So I had a dingy look for the rest of the day. Overall, I would recommend this product to any who was trying to whiten their teeth with out the huge bill.

data.text:
I have had horrific canker sores since I was a kid. They would last for weeks, and I could barely eat because the pain was so bad. Then I stopped using SLS based toothpastes and it changed my life. I went from huge canker sores that would leave scars in my mouth, to only a few mild ones per year.

I used to use another popular brand, specifically made for canker sore sufferers, but they stopped making it. This is the best alternative that I have found.

I do want to mention that there is nothing specifically wrong with SLS, just that some people, like me, have a strong autoimmune response to it which causes canker sores. Search for articles on it if you want to learn more.

data.text: I was lucky to receive a full size tube of Crest Pro-Health Toothpaste- Fresh Clean Mint for free from Smiley 360. I wanted to share my opinion of the product to give insight into how effective it has been for me personally. I am a huge advocate for amazing dental hygiene and strive to always get a thumbs-up at each and every dentist appointment. This toothpaste is actually the multi-tasker of all toothpastes without a doubt. Many toothpastes will claim they can whiten teeth or help with sensitivity or help with tartar or keep your breath fresh and more. This toothpaste does all of these things and exceeded my expectations. I have sensitive teeth and this absolutely worked better than the brand I was using prior to this.  I had no problems eating anything that was too cold at all so it filled my need for sensitivity protection. In my profession I always need to make a great impression and because I smile a lot I value the ability to whiten my teeth with a toothpaste that covers my other needs too. data.title: Gel, thick consistency; mild minty taste; quality ingredients gentle on my sensitive gums.
data.text:
This toothpaste product (Fresh Aid, Sensitive Teeth & Gum health) consists of 3 individually boxed toothpaste tubes.

Each 4-oz toothpaste tube has a flip-top cap, and when I removed the cap, has a foil seal covering the opening.

I smelled a pleasing mild minty scent as I held an opened tube to my nose.
The toothpaste is a gel with a thick consistency and a green-yellowish color.

There is just a little bubbles/suds forming as I brushed my teeth.
I did not have any unpleasant aftertaste when I am done brushing my teeth.

The quality ingredients (including aloe vera, ginger, sunflower seed oil, etc) and its lack of irritating ingredients (such as sodium lauryl sulfate) make this a toothpaste that is gentle on my sensitive gums.

The disadvantage of a toothpaste without fluoride is that it doesn't help with cavity prevention.

Expiration date is on the bottom of the box, as well as at the bottom of each tube (in the creased section). Mine expires October 2022.

This Fresh Aid toothpaste is a decent back-up option when I run out of my preferred brand that not only deals with my sensitive gums but also repairs my weak enamel (with its sodium fluoride ingredient).

data.title: Absolutely Horrified!!
data.text:
I've been using Crest Pro-Health for several years now, and have had white film and mouth sores almost every day. Thinking it was just a residue from the toothpaste, and sores from a possible nervous habit. I was shocked and appalled when my dentist identified the sloughing of skin, due to this toothpaste! I was even more appalled to Google the symptoms and find THOUSANDS of hits, each with THOUSANDS of the same complaints, many indicating P&G denying any such problem exists.

DO NOT USE THIS PRODUCT, it is apparently defective, and probably dangerous IMHO. P&G should be shut down by the FDA for such a damaging product. I will certainly never use it again, and I have been a loyal Crest user since childhood. I will have to think long and hard before trying a P&G product ever again. If this is the way they put out a flagship product, what kind of quality should we expect from their other products?

I also found out that this "Whitening" product actually has been CAUSING the brown staining of my teeth. DO NOT USE THIS PRODUCT!!!

data.title: If your wondering about, this is my first take.
data.text:
I had seen an add for this product via social media. As my picture shows, I have two other products that advertise for the most part instant visible results. Well...

Overall, the product seems to have similar to no difference from normal toothpaste. Nor a huge change in the whiteness of my teeth as shown in the add. Not mad, its an add and its meaning is go get you to buy the product. Well played.

To be fair, Ive only used this product for the last couple of days and truth be told. Didnt always have the best habit when it comes to brushing my teeth twice a day. I was also worried about the products makeup, due to the lack of info on it.

After using the product. The foam it creates is similar to if you were to rinse after with hydrogen peroxide. It does have a nice taste in comparison to the other products as well and less of a mess on your counter top. Another plus is the charcoal is a mess if/when used. Almost feel like I need to brusb twice after using either of the other two.

If your interested and you have a dentist you see on somewhat of a normal time frame. I would either ask them about it and see what they say. Or if the price is right for you and you have tried other things like myself. Id say give it a try.

Hope this helps and you have a wonderful smile!

data.title: Finally figured out that Crest Pro Health is causing my slime!
data.text:
No drama here, this toothpaste does literally peel off a thin layer on all gum surfaces, and it peels off in a slime. I spend a half hour in the morning, after brushing, getting the slime out of my mouth or it gums up into yucky little blobs. Two months ago I had 4 impacted wisdom teeth removed and at the same time I happened to buy Crest Pro Health. I had been attributing my problems to my surgery, but eventually I realized that my surgery was completely healed and through a process of elimination, it was the Crest Pro Health. My husband is always complaining that my breath smells like chemicals and he was concerned that my surgeon had left something "medical" in my gums! But that is not the case.

I have always liked Crest products, but it seems that this one in particular has some problems. I don't even want to know what kind of ingredient/chemical is causing the skin to peel off. It seems iffy enough, to probably avoid this product, until it has been around for a few more years and more problems are noticed.

I have not noticed any staining, but I also do not have any plaque on my teeth at this time.

And my mouth and breath never tastes fresh and clean with this toothpaste. I feel self concious about it even right after brushing, as if I hadn't brushed at all!

data.title: I LOVED LOVED LOVED the old formula which contained more xylitol ...
data.text: Beware!  The formula was recently changed.  Very MISLEADING, THE PACKAGING SHOULD SAY NEW FORMULA.  I LOVED LOVED LOVED the old formula which contained more xylitol which was great at preventing cavities.  The new formula has a thinner consistency, BAD taste, and weird after taste.  It contains more glycerin which is probably cheaper than xylitol.  Glycerin gives it a pasty feel and acts as a barrier on teeth which is HARD to wash off.  It now contains erythritol which Dr. Axe lists as one of the 5 Worst Artificial Sweeteners.  I even called the company and was told they were getting negative feedback.  Shouldn't companies be making products MORE healthy, not less so?  This buyer, once loyal to this brand, is saying BAD decision making by SPRY by putting money ahead of a providing a good healthy product.
